calpain activity in neurons contributes to the control and modulation of SNAP-25 protein levels.
calpains contribute to the post-transcriptional down regulation of SNAP25 in neurons, with the highest level of activity observed in fast spiking GABAergic neurons.
calpain activity contributes to SNAP-25 down regulation in cultured GABAergic inter-neurons and is increased in the hippocampus after acute seizures.

the study of the role of calpain in the regulation of the levels of synaptic components in the brain.
the identification and characterization of novel synaptic protein targets of calpain in the CNS.
the role of calpains in the control of synaptic proteins and their potential implication in neurological disorders.

the calpain activity in neurons contributes to the control and down regulation of SNAP 25 levels in neurons and that the level of calpain activation differs in selected neuronal subtypes.
calpains are a class of calcium dependent proteases that cleave SNAP-25 in neurons.
calpains contribute to the control of synaptic proteins levels in neurons, and that the activity of this family of proteases is differentially regulated in different neuronal populations.

calpain is active in the brain and may be involved in regulating synaptic protein levels in the brain.
calpains are active in the brain and may contribute to the regulation of synaptic proteins in a cell-type specific manner.
